summary.headline: Shriram Finance Q2 FY27 PAT rose 59.37% YoY to Rs 3,677.03 crore, with NIM at 9.52% and credit cost up to 2.03%.
summary.overview: Disbursements grew 25.71% YoY to Rs 54,079.02 crore and AUM rose 16.96% YoY and 4.85% QoQ to about Rs 3.29 lakh crore. Net interest income reached Rs 8,661.04 crore, up from Rs 6,266.84 crore a year ago, and cost-to-income improved to 22.52%. Asset quality softened: gross stage 3 rose to 4.65% and credit cost to 2.03%, which management attributed mainly to drought and monsoon disruption in certain geographies and a denominator effect in construction equipment. Cost of funds fell 15 bps QoQ to 8.41%, and the company declared an interim dividend of Rs 6.5 per share.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Stage 2 and stage 3 rose, which management attributed to customers not servicing monthly interest on time; management plans customer education and cited a target to double the gold book share from about 2.5% to about 5% over three years. LTV is about 72-73%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Disbursements rose to about Rs 10,000 crore in Q2 from about Rs 7,500 crore in the prior peak and about Rs 6,000 crore in recent quarters, as the company expanded into larger geographies beyond the south. Stress is attributed to affected regions, and ticket sizes are rising where comfort exists.

segments.name: Construction equipment
segments.commentary: Disbursements have bounced back, but stage 2 and stage 3 percentages rose; management said absolute gross stage 3 fell to 8.62% from 8.74% and stage 2 rose only to 963 from 953 (management described it as a denominator effect).

segments.name: Passenger and commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Management said new-vehicle contribution breakup will be shared offline; yield differential between new and used vehicles is 200-400 bps depending on segment. Credit cost guidance is elevated for this and next quarter in certain geographies.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 credit cost guidance: management referred to around 2.3% (analyst-stated), up from about 2% previously; the company said credit cost will be temporarily elevated for Q2 and Q3.
FY27 AUM growth guidance cut to about 15-17% from 18% earlier (per analyst recap; management did not dispute it), citing monsoon-related caution in certain geographies.
Cost of borrowings expected to stay around 8.4%; incremental cost of funds expected below 8%, rising to around 8.35% if rate hikes and capital market rates move up.
NIM expected to stay elevated for one to two quarters, then decline to a medium-term level of around 9%; long-term level of around 8.5% referenced by management.
Insurance commission income of about Rs 350 crore; proposed IRDAI circular could impact about Rs 100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did stage 2 and stage 3 rise across construction equipment, gold and MSME, and what is the full-year credit cost outlook versus the earlier guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase is largely due to monsoon and drought-related income disruption in certain geographies; full-year credit cost is now guided around 2.3% vs about 2% earlier, with temporary elevation of 30-40 bps in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How should NIM and cost of funds evolve, and what is the incremental borrowing cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of borrowings on book is 8.4%, incremental cost expected below 8%, rising to about 8.35% if rates and capital market yields rise; medium-term NIM about 9% and longer-term about 8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MSME disbursements jump to about Rs 10,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a focus on larger geographies beyond the south and to a combination of geographic expansion and higher ticket sizes where comfort exists.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gold GS2 and GS3 rising, and is it specific to the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customers who moved to EMI structures are not servicing monthly interest on time; it is addressing this through customer education, and said the trend will stabilise. It did not give a breakup of fresh versus existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15-17% AUM growth guidance conservative, and is the company tightening credit filters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is cautious in certain geographies because of monsoon impact, not because of tighter credit filters; the cut is driven by that caution. It did not quantify the geographic mix beyond Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana being the largest states.

qa_highlights.question: Has excess liquidity been used, and is borrowing picking up?
qa_highlights.answer: Company borrowed about Rs 27,000 crore in the quarter, liquidity brought down to about three months of future repayments, and the borrowing programme will continue as before with no excess liquidity left.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the proposed IRDAI circular on insurance income?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance commission income was about Rs 350 crore; the proposed guidance could cut about Rs 100 crore, which management said is not material to the balance sheet.

capex_capacity: Construction equipment disbursements have bounced back, with management citing rising equipment sales and demand pickup; no capacity or capex figures were given.

Gold loan book was about Rs 9,000 crore (pre-dominantly gold per management remark) and the company is expanding through exclusive gold branches; the target is to double gold share from about 2.5% to about 5% of the book over three years, with no change to that plan.

Company restarted its borrowing programme in Q2 FY27, raising about Rs 27,000 crore in the quarter; liquidity was run down to roughly three months of future repayment obligations, leaving no excess liquidity.
Technology cost to rise for NIMO/new-platform spend, which management said may weigh on cost-to-AUM optics; no amount was quantified.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 disbursements Rs 54,079.02 crore, up 25.71% YoY from Rs 43,019.17 crore; AUM Rs 3,29,002 crore, up 16.96% YoY and 4.85% QoQ.

MSME disbursements about Rs 10,000 crore in Q2 vs about Rs 7,500 crore at prior peak and about Rs 6,000 crore in recent quarters; growth driven by expansion beyond southern markets and rising ticket sizes where comfort exists.
Management said demand picked up in the last month for some products but it turned cautious on certain products due to monsoon impact; FY27 AUM growth guidance trimmed to about 15-17% from 18%.
Gold loan LTV about 72-73%; gold disbursement in the prior quarter was Rs 5,153 crore (per management).
Yield differential between new and used vehicles 200-400 bps depending on segment; new-vehicle breakup to be shared offline.

Cost of borrowings on book 8.41% (down 15 bps QoQ); incremental cost of funds 7.3% vs 7.7% prior quarter; cost of funds expected to stay around 8.4%, incremental below 8% for now, rising to about 8.35% if rates and capital market rates move up.
risks_watch: Stage 3 rose to 4.65% gross and credit cost to 2.03%, with management guiding temporary elevation in Q2 and Q3 and full-year credit cost around 2.3%, implying a second-half run-rate above 2.4%.
Gold loan stage 2 and stage 3 rising because customers are not servicing monthly interest; management has not shown when this stabilises.
NIM is guided to stay elevated for one to two quarters and then fall toward about 9% medium term, with the risk that rate hikes and capital market rates push the cost of funds higher.
AUM growth guidance cut to 15-17% from 18%; monitor whether monsoon-related caution spreads across geographies.
Insurance commission income at risk of about Rs 100 crore if the proposed IRDAI circular is implemented; management said the impact on the balance sheet is not material.
Limited disclosure: management did not provide geographic breakdowns of stress or the share of unsecured MSME exposure, and deferred several questions to offline follow-ups.
key_quotes: We registered disbursement growth of 25.71% year on year.
Our cost to income ratio was 22.52% in Q2 FY27 as against 27.76% recorded in Q2 FY26.
The cost of libraries on balance sheet is 8.41% versus 8.56% in the previous quarter, reduction of 15 basis point and from March it is down by 18 basis point.

The flooding is something very normal in the monsoon season it will not have any negative impact so temporary some two three days impact will be there that will not impact the overall economic activity.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on borrowing costs, liquidity and the medium-term cost-to-income target, but cautious and often vague on asset quality drivers and on growth guidance, attributing stress to monsoon and drought disruption and deferring several granular questions to offline follow-up.

adds.what: Exclusive gold branches expanding gold loan book (target to double gold share from about 2.5% to about 5% over three years); no branch count or capex given

growth.why: FY27 AUM growth guidance cut to about 15-17% from 18% (midpoint 16%) citing monsoon caution; growth backed by disbursement momentum (+25.71% YoY) and MSME expansion beyond south, but no specific capacity, orders or capex figures, and gold branch expansion lacks numbers, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM at 9.52% is guided to stay elevated for one to two quarters, then fall toward about 9% medium term and about 8.5% longer term, so margin expansion is not expected.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Exclusive gold branches are expanding the gold book (about Rs 9,000 crore, target 5% of book in three years), but no branch count or capex was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Disbursements grew 25.71% YoY to Rs 54,079 crore and AUM grew 16.96% YoY, but FY27 AUM growth guidance was cut to 15-17% from 18%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex figures or plans were given; the company is funding growth through borrowings of about Rs 27,000 crore in Q2 rather than capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 AUM growth guidance was cut to 15-17% from 18% and full-year credit cost was raised to around 2.3% from about 2%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost is guided to rise 30-40 bps temporarily in Q2 and Q3, with full-year around 2.3% implying a second-half run-rate above 2.4%, and AUM growth was already cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launches were discussed; gold branch expansion and the MSME push into new geographies are existing initiatives.

rows.label: Medium-term cost-to-income of about 25%
rows.why: Cost-to-income improved to 22.52% from 27.76% a year ago, and management guided a medium-term level of about 25%, though NIMO technology spend will weigh on cost-to-AUM.

rows.label: Liquidity rebuilt via Rs 27,000 crore borrowing
rows.why: Company raised about Rs 27,000 crore in Q2 and liquidity is down to about three months of repayments, so the borrowing programme continues with no excess liquidity.

rows.label: Cost of funds falling, incremental below 8%
rows.why: Cost of borrowings fell 15 bps QoQ to 8.41% and incremental cost is 7.3%, but it could rise to about 8.35% if rates rise.

tone.note: Management was confident on borrowing costs, liquidity and the 25% medium-term cost-to-income target, but cautious and vague on asset quality drivers such as gold GS2/GS3 and on the AUM growth cut, deferring granular questions offline; analysts pressed on credit cost, gold stress and growth guidance

oneOffs.what: Stage 3 and credit cost rise (credit cost 2.03% vs 1.68% in Q2 FY26) from monsoon/drought disruption and gold-loan interest non-servicing; management guides 30-40 bps temporary elevation in Q2 and Q3,
Year-ago Q2 FY26 profit base (Rs 2,307.18 crore) is not described in the brief as weak or disrupted, so no low-base adjustment is applied

quality.why: Growth is driven by volume: disbursements rose 25.71% YoY to Rs 54,079 crore and AUM rose 16.96% YoY, with NIM expanding to 9.52% from 8.19%, lifting NII about 38%; PAT growth of 59% is flattered by margin and cost-to-income gains, while credit cost rising to 2.03% (from 1.68%) and temporary elevation guided for Q2 and Q3 will weigh on the recurring profit run-rate.
